title: Chapter 58 — The Account Review: Diagnostics, Share & Leakage
intro: The quarterly ritual — the share question, leakage diagnostics, and the review meeting.

sections.title: The Share Question
sections.content:
Revenue tells you how much an account is spending with you. Share tells you how much they are spending with everyone else. The single most important account metric is share — because share exposes leakage that revenue hides.

If a builder does 20 projects a year at $5,000 average and you handle 8, your share is 40 percent. That means 12 projects — $60,000 in revenue — is going to your competitor. The share question is: why?

sections.title: Leakage Diagnostics
sections.content:
Pull up the account data. How many projects did they do this quarter? How many came through you? What categories are you winning — and which ones are going elsewhere?

Common leakage patterns: they use you for cooking but buy laundry elsewhere. They use you for mid-range but go to a competitor for luxury. They use you for retail customers but have a separate trade supplier for volume projects.

Each pattern tells you where to focus. The account review is not a courtesy meeting — it is a diagnostic session.

sections.title: The Review Meeting
sections.content:
Quarterly. In person if possible. Bring the data.

'Your volume is up 15 percent this quarter — great. I noticed we handled 8 of your 12 projects. I would love to earn the other 4. What would need to change for you to consolidate with us?'

Listen to the answer. It might be pricing. It might be a specific brand you do not carry. It might be delivery flexibility. Whatever it is, that is your action item for next quarter.
